assessment: Pixel review supports HOLD. The radius-one-pixel target aperture retains positive box depths of 3.694 +/- 0.822, 2.076 +/- 0.355 and 5.740 +/- 0.827 ppt in sectors 60, 74 and 75 [M], but the folds have broad, changing structure rather than a stable isolated transit. The difference images do not identify a unique source, and background changes confound a simple centroid interpretation. The pixel follow-up does not resolve the nearby-source ambiguity or the poorly constrained fit geometry. No additional clean EB report is justified.
what_would_change: To reconsider: independently reproduce a repeated localized transit while fitting the variable sky/background and nearby sources, and obtain useful transit-geometry uncertainties.
scope: Final local pixel assessment, retained after the main coordinator completed C and refreshed all six Stage D catalogues. No external submission was made.

figures.caption: Primary and phase-0.5 difference images at the accepted physical-fit ephemeris; Gaia positions are propagated to the sector epoch.

Fixed target aperture and sky variations, full phase and transit windows after sky subtraction. All sectors use the same aperture and background geometry. The Gaia mask uses a 300-arcsec cone covering the target aperture and background annulus.

background_mask_review.scope: Supplied Gaia sources on the cutout use the same fixed mask geometry. The 300-arcsec cone covers the target aperture and the background annulus, including the two-pixel source-exclusion margin; full corner coverage of a 21-by-21-pixel square is not required for that annulus.
background_mask_review.outcome: Both rerendered figures inspected; assessment unchanged. No aperture radius, ephemeris, detrending or science gate was tuned.
